requirements.requirement: Node1 runs an internal DNS resolver that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2.
requirements.summary: BIND was installed from the RHEL 9 repositories, its configuration and internal zone validated, and named was enabled and listening on node1. Direct queries returned node2's address, 10.100.93.11. A node1 restart changed its boot identity, after which named, the listener, zone serial, firewall access, and a client lookup all recovered successfully.

requirements.requirement: Node2 uses node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups and successfully resolves the required name to node2.
requirements.summary: Node2's persistent NetworkManager profile and live resolver both identify node1 at 10.100.93.10. End-to-end resolution returned node2's own managed address, 10.100.93.11. After node2 restarted with a changed boot identity, the persistent profile, live resolver, NetworkManager service, and lookup all recovered.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes began and ended on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64. BIND 9.16 packages were installed from the platform's official RHEL 9 repositories, and package-health checks remained successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service/configuration and lookup behavior.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots inventory temporary files but not /etc, so they do not independently establish whether /etc/named.conf.antrieb-before was removed or retained after successful completion. No evidence indicates that this affected functionality or hygiene.

No independent post-executor package inventory was captured, although the successful RHEL-repository installation, recovered named service, unchanged platform, and healthy package-manager consistency checks provide strong evidence of compatibility.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, DNS configuration, service enablement, the scoped firewall rule, and NetworkManager changes were directly required by the task; sequential reboots and transient systemd scheduling supported the mandatory restart protocol. Failed commands occurred only while nodes were rebooting and do not show unwanted mutation. Final snapshots show healthy package state, no failed services, only the intended DNS exposure on node1, and no unexpected node2 listeners. The named.conf backup created by cmd-59a089e53b0f4213 had a clear rollback-safety role and is not treated as unnecessary, although its eventual retention was not observed.
